title: Ticket Table Solved Each Team Before Comparing
text: id: COMP-011 domain: math title: Ticket Table Solved Each Team Before Comparing tags: table, comparison, tickets memory: A support dashboard question once fooled me because I compared teams before finishing their individual ledgers. I gave Team A its own start, closed, received calculation, then did the same for Team B. Only then did I total and compare. I wrote which team had more and the exact ticket difference, because the table was not finished until the comparison had a number.

title: Ticket Comparison Needed The Difference In Tickets
text: id: COMP-024 domain: math title: Ticket Comparison Needed The Difference In Tickets tags: tickets, comparison, difference, table memory: I once finished a ticket table with the totals but forgot the comparison the user had asked for. The corrected answer named the team with more and gave the difference in tickets. If Team A had 10 and Team B had 11, the visible final line had to read: Team B has more by 1 ticket. The comparison was not commentary; it was part of the result.

title: Ratio Mixture Counted Total Parts Before Liters
text: id: COMP-009 domain: math title: Ratio Mixture Counted Total Parts Before Liters tags: ratio, mixture, parts memory: A mixture ratio felt like two numbers competing until I counted total parts. Two parts and five parts made seven parts total, and I wrote total volume divided by total parts to find liters per part. Only then did I multiply by each side of the ratio. The concentrate and water added back to the requested total.
